- Extensions are not allowed; work must be submitted by the expiration date.

Q: Do colleges and universities require a student's class rank on their admissions' paperwork?

Colleges and universities consider a variety of factors in their admission decisions. According to the National Association for College Admission Counseling (NACAC), the top factors in the admission decision are (1) Grades in college prep courses; (2) Strength of curriculum; and (3) Admission test scores.

How to Get Started

Students work with their Texas Tech K-12 advisor to determine eligibility, select appropriate college courses and ensure coursework aligns with their academic and graduation goals.

Once approved, students apply as dual credit students, enroll in their selected Texas Tech University courses and begin building their college transcript.

Q: Without having a class rank, what factors are most important for college admissions?

Without a class rank, college admissions officers will look more closely at applications and high school transcripts. Without a class rank, college admissions officers will look more closely at applications and high school transcripts. Important factors will include the following: maintaining a high grade point average, college entrance exams (SAT and ACT), challenging school course selections, extracurricular involvement, college application essays, and personal recommendations.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants.When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

query.raw: Where can the course catalog be located on the Focus portal?

chunks.text:
Focus Dashboard

After successfully logging into the portal, you will be taken to your Dashboard that shows My Active Courses. The dashboard is your starting point into managing your profile, accessing courses, reviewing the course catalog, utilizing forms and downloads, and contacting Texas Tech K-12.

Focus Portal Homepage

The Focus Portal Homepage is where you will be able to view your "Information", access "Communication", update "Preferences, view your "Class Schedule", access your final "Grade(s) and any "Forms". From this page, you will also be able to access Canvas.

Accessing the Texas Tech K-12 Focus Portal

To begin, access the new Texas Tech K-12 Portal through a web browser. This portal uses single sign-on (SSO), allowing you to access your courses directly without logging into the Learning Management System (LMS) separately.

Navigate to the Texas Tech K-12 Focus Portal.

Enter your username and password.

Click Log in to access your dashboard.

Once logged in, the dashboard will serve as your home base for managing students, viewing profiles, and accessing course content.

Note: If you encounter login issues, ensure your credentials are correct. After five unsuccessful attempts, your account will be locked for two hours.

Focus Portal

The Focus Portal is where you will login. The portal may be access by visiting the Focus Portal (opens in new tab).

Please note that upon login, you will be taken to your Focus Homepage

How do I access my final course grade?

Final course grades will be posted to the student's Focus account under "Grades".

Please note the following:

· Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Students: A final grade will be recorded on his/her official Texas Tech K-12 transcript as well as posted in the student's portal. Full-time students may request a copy of their transcript from inside of Focus, or via the transcript request (opens in new tab).

· Non Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Students: Students and parents may view the final course grade on the portal. It is the student’s responsibility to very that the grade is received and recorded on their official school transcript.

· Homeschool Students: Final grades may be viewed on the portal. Grade Reports may be printed from the portal.

· We have received some reports of School Counselors and students not being able to access the Adobe PDF copy of the grade report. We ask that you please ensure that you are using Google Chrome and that in your extensions, that the Adobe Acrobat extension is currently enabled. We also ask that you please ensure that your current Adobe setting is set to “Covert Current web page to an Adobe PDF File has access to this site. If these settings are not enabled, we ask that you please check with your School or District IT to ensure that the extensions are enabled.

How do I get started with a Course or Credit By Exam (CBE)?

Available Courses and Credit By Exam's may be viewed via the Course Catalog (opens in new tab). Prior to enrolling, we ask that you please confirm with your local school that they will award credit for the course. Upon completion of the course, student's will be ale to view the overall course grade in the portal. You may also print out a copy of the grade report.

Focus Homepage

The Focus Homepage is the landing page once you have logged into the Focus Portal. Upon logging in, the Homepage serves as your central hub providing access to:

Step 1: Students

Step 2: Users

Step 3: Scheduling

Step 4: Grades

Step 5: Assessments

Step 6: Forms

How do I get started with a Course or Credit By Exam (CBE)?

Available Courses and Credit By Exam's may be viewed via the Course Catalog (opens in new tab). Prior to enrolling, we ask that you please confirm with your local school that they will award credit for the course. Upon completion of the course, student's will be ale to view the overall course grade in the portal. You may also print out a copy of the grade report.

Counselor Portal: Log in to Focus Student Information System

Go to the Focus Student Information System login page: Focus Student Information System Login (opens in new tab). Enter your username and password, then press Log in.

Export grade reports — Counselor Portal (Focus Student Information System)

Counselors can export grade reports from the Grades tab once a course has a final grade posted. To do so, simply click the Grade Report button to generate the report. Please note that reports can only be exported one course at a time; there is currently no option to export multiple courses simultaneously.

If you don’t see the option to print a grade report for a completed course, switch the view to “View Detailed Report.” Once the page refreshes, the grade report will be available.

Focus Dashboard — Counselor Portal

After successfully logging into the portal, you will be taken to your Dashboard. The Dashboard is your starting point into viewing student count and student information, your profile, accessing reports on course grades and student activity, and contacting Texas Tech K-12.

Counselor Portal — My Profile (primary info & attached students)

The My Profile page will allow you to view your Primary Information, see attached students and view general information about your account.

First Time Access (Creating An Account)

Students, if you have not created your account, please visit our Student Registration (opens in new tab) page. The student portal will allow you to access your courses, monitor your course progress in school by providing timely access to both assignments and grades that are entered by your teacher throughout the grading period. You will also have the ability to contact your teacher via the "Communications" module inside of Focus.

In order to create your account, you must have a valid email address. Please note that the email address should not be the same as another student's email or your parent's email.

Texas Tech K-12 offers several different programs (each program is listed below). Based upon your selection, application requirements may be different:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) - If you will remain enrolled at your local school, you must obtain prior approval from your school counselor before enrolling in any course or CBE. Failure to obtain approval may result in un-awarded credit for a course or CBE. With prior approval, students enrolled in another school may enroll in:

Step 2: Supplemental courses (opens in new tab)

Step 3: Credit-by-Examinations or CBE's (opens in new tab).

Step 4: Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Student - If you are withdrawing from your local school district and wish to become a Full-Time Student at Texas Tech K-12, you may apply to:

Step 5: The "Tuition-Free Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Texas Residents), or

Step 6: The "Tuition-Paid Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Outside of Texas or Texas Residents seeking more flexibility).

Step 7: College Preparatory Academy (opens in new tab) - Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time students may earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. These courses are typically offered through partnerships between high schools and colleges or universities, enabling students to get a head start on their college education while still in high school.
